name: report ground truth
summary: The answer key for the capstone report: the claims a defensible brief on Operator Alpha should make, each with the TYPE (fact/assessment/assumption) and CONFIDENCE (high/moderate/low) the chained evidence actually supports. A report is graded not on whether it states the findings — assembling the facts is the easy part — but on whether it preserves their sourcing and calibration. The dangerous error is OVERCLAIMING: presenting a claim more strongly than the evidence licenses (an assessment as a fact, a low- or moderate-confidence judgement as high) or with no provenance to check.

notes: Six claims are supported at high confidence, one (rebrand) at moderate, one (timezone) at low; two (follow_through, clone) are facts, the rest assessments. A naive assembler that flattens every claim to a sourceless high-confidence fact still covers all eight but strips all provenance, miscalibrates the moderate and low claims, and overclaims every assessment it presents as fact.
